explanations: luna: The same warning boundary appears here: disbelievers do not believe whether the Prophet warns them or not, unlike the section’s protected, fearful recipient.
luna: After 2:6’s rejected warning, hearts and hearing are sealed; it gives a concrete blockage opposite the section’s alarm that should reach and move its hearers.

luna: The source-section root ن و ر explains نار through flickering light; here a kindled fire first lights the surroundings and then its light is taken away. It is a different parable and a tentative lexical contrast with the section’s punitive flame. | terra: A kindled fire first illuminates its surroundings, then God removes their light; this directly exposes the section's dictionary link between fire and trembling light while showing that illumination need not become guidance.

luna: The command اتقوا النار directly joins the source-section’s root و ق ي, protective fear, to the very fire that 92:14 warns about. | terra: فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلنَّارَ commands people to place the section's protective taqwā between themselves and a fire fueled by people and stones.
luna: The Prophet is sent as a warner, and the verse names the companions of Hell; it joins the warning role to the fire outcome in the section.
terra: The disowned followers see their deeds as regrets and are not coming out of the fire, giving permanent consequence to a failure that no later precaution can undo.
terra: فَمَآ أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ ironically asks how they can endure the fire after trading guidance away, closely touching the section's sense of suffering and remaining under its heat.

luna: The prayer قنا عذاب النار asks to be kept safe from Fire, a concise response to the section’s alarm. | terra: The prayer وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ turns the shield root into a direct request that God ward off fire.
terra: The polytheists call toward the fire whereas God calls toward the Garden and forgiveness, exposing two rival summons and the destination reached by answering each.

luna: Believers ask God to protect them from the punishment of Fire, showing divine shielding as the answer to the section’s warning. | terra: Believers ask وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ after confessing faith, another explicit appeal for the divine side of the section's protection.

luna: This repeats the command to guard against the prepared Fire, a direct Quranic formulation of the section’s protective barrier. | terra: وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكَافِرِينَ is a second direct imperative to put protective heed between oneself and a prepared fire.

luna: People report that an enemy force has gathered against the believers; the report increases their faith, and they rely on God. This closely matches the section’s alarm of an approaching enemy and the response of taking precautions.
luna: The believers return with favor and no harm touches them, completing the response to the warning in 3:173 and echoing the section’s protection from danger.

luna: Being moved far from the Fire and admitted to the Garden is called success, a direct outcome for the section’s protected person. | terra: فَمَن زُحْزِحَ عَنِ ٱلنَّارِ stages salvation as being physically edged away from the fire, clarifying the section's causative “will be kept to the side.”
terra: Those who remember God عَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ pray فَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ; bodily “sides,” the place of the section's shield-name, meet the explicit request for protection from fire.
terra: The prayer says that whoever God admits into the fire is disgraced and has no helpers, clarifying admission as the opposite of being warded and moved aside.

luna: Those who consume orphan wealth unjustly are said to eat fire and burn in the Blaze; this joins misuse of wealth to the source section’s wealth-hoarder and fire fate. | terra: Those who consume orphan wealth unjustly consume fire into their bellies and will burn in a blaze, joining wrongful acquisition, internalized fire, and the section's ص ل ي action.
terra: One who commits the prohibited act in aggression and injustice is promised admission to fire, another direct use of the section's burning-entry root with the conduct that leads there.

luna: Disbelievers are burned in the Fire and their skins replaced so they continue tasting punishment, a direct instance of the source-section’s root ص ل ي and its enduring fire. | terra: The skins of those burned in fire are repeatedly replaced so that they continue to taste punishment, concretizing the section's gloss of enduring the fire's heat and severity.
luna: The command to take precautions and advance in groups gives another concrete military form of the source section’s warning about an enemy advance and the precautions that should follow.
luna: The source-section’s warning example is an enemy advance that should make hearers take precautions; here the fighters take حذرهم and weapons because the enemy may attack while they pray.
terra: One who opposes the messenger after guidance is clear and follows another way is turned toward that choice and burned in Hell, directly joining a deviating route to fiery arrival.
terra: Those who disbelieve and do wrong are denied guidance to a way, setting up 4:169's sole remaining path to Hell and tying rejection to misdirection.
terra: The only path left to the deniers is the path of Hell, where they remain, closely paralleling the section's twisted course that terminates in fire.
terra: The condemned want to emerge from the fire but cannot and have lasting punishment, making the absence of any effective escape the reverse of being kept away beforehand.
luna: The command فاجتنبوه tells people to avoid harmful practices and promises success; it is the active avoiding sense of the source-section root ج ن ب.
luna: The Prophet is told that the Quran warns its hearers and whoever it reaches; this specifies how the section’s alarm travels from one voice to its audience.
terra: At the gathering, the people allied with jinn are assigned the fire as their abode; 6:130 later asks whether messengers warned them of this very meeting.

terra: The gathered communities are asked whether messengers recited the signs and warned them of their meeting that day, and they testify against themselves; it supplies the acknowledged alarm behind 6:128's fire.
terra: After literal clothing that covers nakedness, لِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ is called best; this turns the section's naked signal and its taqwā-shield into two sides of one clothing image.
terra: Adam's children are warned that Satan stripped their parents' clothing; beside 7:26's garment of taqwā, the lost covering becomes a caution about allowing the protective layer to be removed.
terra: Messengers recount God's signs, and whoever takes protective heed and reforms has no fear; the ayah supplies the successful response before 7:36 gives the denier's fiery result.
terra: Those who deny the signs and act arrogantly toward them become abiding companions of the fire, completing 7:35's warning-and-taqwā alternative.
terra: Hell is both a bed beneath and coverings above the wrongdoers; the layers that would ordinarily shelter instead become fire.
luna: Noah asks whether his people wonder that a reminder came through one of them to warn them, so they may fear and receive mercy; the alarm has a protective aim.
luna: They denied Noah, so he and the believers were saved while the deniers drowned; it gives a concrete division between response to warning and its rejection.

terra: The community is told to take protective heed of a trial that will not strike only the wrongdoers, extending taqwā from personal fear to precaution against a danger that can overrun a whole group.
luna: The command to prepare strength against an enemy is a specific parallel to the section’s example of learning of an assault and making oneself ready.

luna: The verse condemns hoarding gold and silver without spending it; this is the same gather-and-hoard figure whom Leza calls in the section’s cited 70:18. | terra: Those who hoard gold and silver are told to expect painful punishment; this is the explicit alarm before 9:35 heats their hoard in Hell and brands their sides.

luna: The hoarded wealth is heated in Hell and brands foreheads, sides, and backs; the source-section root ج ن ب also names a shield by the side, here reversed into an exposed side scorched by fire. | terra: Hoarded metal is heated in Hell and brands foreheads, جُنُوبُهُمْ, and backs; the bodily “side” that explains the shield-name in the section becomes exposed to fire when wealth is hoarded rather than given.
terra: A building founded on taqwā is set against a crumbling bank that falls with its builder into Hellfire, making the protective layer and the twisted route to fire into rival structures.
luna: The source-section root ص ل ي includes roasting meat; Abraham’s calf is described as حنيذ, a roasted meal, giving that secondary fire sense a hospitable rather than punitive scene.
luna: The source-section root ش ق و names wretchedness opposite happiness; this judgment divides people into شَقِيّ and سعيد before specifying their ends.

luna: This identifies the wretched party from 11:105 as being in the fire, where they sigh and sob; it joins the section’s ashqa label directly to its flame. | terra: فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ شَقُوا۟ فَفِى ٱلنَّارِ directly places those marked by شقوة in the fire, confirming the section's lexical joining of wretchedness and burning.

luna: The source-section root ص ل ي includes remaining in the fire; this verse says the wretched abide there with sighing and sobbing, subject to God’s will. | terra: The wretched remain there as long as the heavens and earth endure, elaborating the section's gloss of صلي as entering the fire and staying with it.

luna: The happy party’s lasting Garden answers the section’s contrast between the wretch who enters and the most mindful person kept away. | terra: Opposite 11:106's ٱلَّذِينَ شَقُوا۟, ٱلَّذِينَ سُعِدُوا۟ are in the Garden; this is the Quranic realization of the section's dictionary claim that wretchedness is the contrary of happiness.
terra: Joseph's interpretation instructs sustained sowing and protected storage before the announced famine, a specific nonlexical parallel to warning becoming complete through practical precaution.
terra: The seven hard years then consume what was stored except a protected remainder, showing why the advance measures ordered in 12:47 constitute an effective shield.

terra: Material heated in fire for ornaments or tools throws off scum; although no punishment is involved, this is a Quranic instance of fire used by a craftsperson to work material, illuminating the section's secondary ص ل ي sense.
terra: The wrongdoers have no وَاقٍ from God, stating the absence of precisely the protecting agent promised to the section's wary person.
terra: Those who exchange God's favor for disbelief lead their people to ruin, Hell, which they enter and burn in; misdirection by a leader ends in the section's ص ل ي action.

terra: Abraham asks God to keep him and his children apart from idol worship; the causative form of ج ن ب shows divine distancing as protection, although the object avoided is an antecedent of punishment rather than the fire itself.
terra: Every nation receives a messenger commanding worship of God and avoidance of false powers; warning and deliberate اجتناب are joined as the path of precaution.

luna: The Quran says clothing protects from heat and violence; the source-section root و ق ي explains taqwa as placing a protective layer against what is feared. | terra: Garments تَقِيكُمُ ٱلْحَرَّ and armor تَقِيكُم بَأْسَكُمْ are literal intervening layers against heat and violence, concretizing both the fire-threat and the dictionary definition of و ق ي.
terra: كُلَّمَا خَبَتْ زِدْنَاهُمْ سَعِيرًا says that whenever Hell's fire subsides it is increased in blaze, giving the section's quick, restless flame an image of continually renewed combustion.
luna: The Book warns of severe punishment while giving good news to believers, joining the section’s alarm and its division between the fire-bound and the protected.
luna: The believers’ abiding reward completes the good-news side introduced alongside warning in 18:2, complementing the section’s fire and shelter contrast.

luna: The wrongdoers are enclosed by a سرادق of fire; this reverses the source-section’s protective barrier, since here a boundary traps rather than shields from the flame. | terra: A fire whose surrounding pavilion encloses the wrongdoers turns a shelter-like boundary into the fire's own wall, the inverse of the section's saving barrier.
terra: The guilty see the fire, know they are about to fall into it, and find no مَصْرِفًا away from it; the missing route of diversion sharpens what وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا grants.
terra: A people report the threat of Gog and Magog and ask for a سَدًّا between the attackers and themselves, reproducing the section's enemy alarm and its required intervening layer.

terra: He asks them to help with strength so that he can place a رَدْمًا between the two sides; this ayah supplies the cooperative precaution that the warning scene requires before 18:96's fire-forging.

terra: Dhul-Qarnayn heats iron until it becomes fire and pours molten copper over it to make the barrier requested in 18:94; this joins the section's fire-as-craft sense to an interposed defense against an approaching enemy.
terra: The attackers can neither scale nor pierce the completed barrier, showing the defensive result of the alarm and the fire-crafted layer in 18:94-96.
terra: God knows which faction is most deserving of burning in Hell; this supplies the ص ل ي action immediately before 19:71's approach and 19:72's rescue of those who took protective heed.

luna: The verse says everyone will come to the Fire, while 19:72 immediately saves those who feared God; its relation to the section’s “only the wretch enters” depends on how وُرُودها is understood, since arrival or passage is also read. | terra: Every person is brought to or passes over Hell before 19:72 distinguishes those God rescues for their taqwā, making divine removal from danger the climax of an actual approach to it.

luna: The next verse says God saves those who feared Him and leaves wrongdoers there; this is a direct instance of the section’s atqa kept away from fire. | terra: ثُمَّ نُنَجِّى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوا۟ says that God rescues those who took protective heed, giving the saving action behind the section's passive وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا.

luna: The source-section root ش ق و includes distress and hardship; here the Quran is explicitly not sent to make the Prophet تَشْقَى, a different use of that root. | terra: مَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِتَشْقَىٰ denies that revelation was sent to make the messenger wretched; the warning is therefore the rescue from شقاء, not its cause.

luna: The Quran is a reminder for one who fears; this clarifies the recipient side of the section’s alarm and the atqa kept from fire. | terra: The revelation is instead a reminder for one who fears, completing 20:2's contrast and matching the section's idea that fear should produce receptive precaution.

luna: The source section’s naked alarm is a visible sign at distance and names نار through the source root ن و ر; here Musa sees a far-off fire and goes toward it for news or a brand. The relation is tentative because this fire guides rather than threatens. | terra: Moses sees a fire at a distance and hopes to bring a brand or find guidance there; as a plausible counter-image, distant fire functions as a visible signal toward guidance rather than the warned destination.
terra: Who comes to God as a criminal has Hell, where he neither dies nor lives; this repeats the enduring-fire condition that the section attaches to entry.

luna: Following God’s guidance means no going astray or being wretched; turning away leads into the hardship-and-fire sequence developed in 20:124–127 and the section’s ashqa contrast. | terra: Who follows God's guidance neither goes astray nor يَشْقَىٰ, making freedom from wretchedness the result of taking the directed path rather than turning from it.

luna: Turning away from remembrance leads to a constricted life; the source section likewise pairs turning away with the route made hard and the fire reached by the wretch. | terra: Who turns away from God's reminder receives a constrained life, tying the section's turning away to lived hardship before the final fire.
luna: This is the turned-away person’s question after being raised blind, continuing the consequence of 20:124’s refusal of remembrance.

luna: The answer says God’s signs came and were forgotten; this names the neglected warning behind the person’s post-resurrection state. | terra: God answers that signs came but were forgotten, supplying the rejected signal that explains the hardship of 20:124 and the loss of guidance in 20:123.
luna: This concludes the refusal sequence by saying the Hereafter’s punishment is more severe and lasting, fitting the section’s warning of the final fire.
terra: The unbelievers cannot يَكُفُّونَ the fire from their faces or backs and receive no help, a direct reversal of the effective shield and divine distancing promised to the wary.
terra: Punishment comes suddenly, stuns them, and they can neither repel it nor gain respite; it is the hostile surprise for which the section's advance alarm and shield are needed.
terra: The messenger says he warns only by revelation, but the deaf do not hear the call إِذَا مَا يُنذَرُونَ; it defines failed warning as a failure to receive and act on the signal.

luna: David is taught armor that protects people from battle; this gives a physical protective counterpart to the source-section’s dictionary image of a shield at one’s side. | terra: God teaches the manufacture of armor لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأْسِكُمْ, turning craft into an intervening protection from hostile force just as the section's shield stands beside a warned person.
luna: Those promised good are kept far away from Hell, an exact parallel to the section’s يُجَنَّبُها for the most mindful.
luna: The saved do not even hear Hell’s hiss, completing the distance from its flame in 21:101.
luna: The greatest terror does not grieve them; this adds the safety from fear that the section’s protection from fire implies.
terra: Garments of fire are cut for the disbelieving party and boiling liquid is poured over their heads, turning an ordinarily protective layer into the punishment itself.
terra: The poured heat melts what is inside their bellies and their skins, specifying the fire's severity before 22:22 describes their failed attempts to leave it.
terra: Whenever they try to leave the fire from anguish they are returned to it, dramatizing the section's gloss that the one made to enter remains attached to the fire.
terra: Fire scorches the condemned faces while they grimace within it; 23:105-106 then identify denial and their own شِقْوَتُنَا, making this the bodily fire-side of that sequence.
terra: They are asked whether God's signs were recited and they used to deny them, supplying the failed reception of warning that leads to the fire in 23:104 and wretchedness in 23:106.
terra: The people in the fire confess غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنَا شِقْوَتُنَا and that they went astray, explicitly joining the section's wretchedness, crooked course, and fiery result.

terra: The lamp's oil nearly glows وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ; light stands at the boundary of fire without being touched by it, a luminous counter-image to the section's fire named from flickering light.
terra: Those who deny the Hour have a blaze prepared for them, placing denial of the warning's horizon immediately before the enraged fire that sees them from afar in 25:12.

luna: The source-section gloss for تلظى includes burning in anger; here the fire sees its inmates from afar and is heard in تَغَيُّظٍ and roaring. | terra: When the blaze sees the condemned from far away they hear its rage and roaring; this Quranic fire is not only hot but angry, exactly developing the section's anger sense of blazing.
luna: The source section distinguishes entering from remaining in fire; here its inmates are thrown into a narrow place in chains, turning the source’s protective barrier into confinement.
luna: This completes the narrow-fire scene of 25:13: the inmates call for one destruction, then many, giving the anguish behind the section’s warning.
luna: This verse calls the Judgment Day عسيرًا for disbelievers; the source section glosses ash-shaqā as hardship and joins the wretch to the difficult end.
luna: The servants pray for God to turn the punishment of Hell away from them; the source-section root ج ن ب describes being moved away from harm.
luna: They call Hell an evil place to settle, completing their plea to be kept away from it in 25:65.
luna: The servants of the Merciful spend neither extravagantly nor stingily; this sharpens the giver-versus-miser contrast that frames the section’s spared and fire-bound people.

luna: Musa tells his family he sees a fire and will bring news or a brand; this repeats the distant visible signal, but reverses the section’s warning fire into guidance. | terra: Moses tells his family he perceives a fire and may return with news or a burning brand for warmth; the specific link is the section's far-visible signal and moving flame, though here the fire promises aid rather than danger.

terra: An ant sees Solomon's host approaching, tells the ants to enter their dwellings, and they take shelter; it is a Quranic enactment of the section's model in which an alarm is completed only by precaution.

luna: Musa sees fire from the mountain’s side and goes to it for news or a burning brand; this is a repeated distant-fire signal, tentatively contrasted with the section’s dangerous flame. | terra: Moses notices fire from the side of the mount and seeks news or an ember; this may echo the section's remotely legible signal, but its narrative role is guidance and warmth, not threatened punishment.
terra: The oppressive leaders are made leaders who call people to the fire, a human counter-call to the warning voice that seeks to move hearers away from it.
terra: وَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمُحِيطَةٌ بِٱلْكَافِرِينَ makes Hell the encompassing layer, reversing taqwā's enclosure against what is feared.
terra: Punishment covers them from above and from beneath their feet, supplying the spatial completion of Hell's encirclement in 29:54.
terra: Their sides leave their beds as they call on God in fear and hope and spend from His provision; the bodily “side” named in the shield gloss meets fear, action, and giving in one posture.
terra: Whenever the defiantly disobedient try to leave the fire they are returned and told to taste what they denied, joining denial, entry, and inescapable residence.
terra: David is told to make full coats of mail and measure their links, another craft scene in which carefully shaped material becomes protection from violence.

luna: The Prophet is told to say he is only a نذير before severe punishment, matching the section’s single first-person alarm before the blazing fire. | terra: The messenger is defined as نَذِيرٌ لَّكُم بَيْنَ يَدَىْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ, a warning voice positioned immediately in front of severe punishment like the section's solitary alarm before the fire.
terra: Satan is an enemy whose party-call aims to make people companions of the blaze, joining the hostile threat, a summons, and fiery destination.

luna: This verse says the disbelievers remain in the Fire without death or relief; the next verse recalls that a warner came, completing the section’s entry-and-warning sequence. | terra: Hell's people are neither finished by death nor granted any lightening of punishment, fully staging the section's sense of entering the fire and remaining under its severity.

luna: Those in the punishment admit a warner did come before being told to taste it; this directly stages the section’s warning refused before fire. | terra: While crying to be released, they are reminded that a lifetime for recollection and a نَذِير came to them; their continued confinement is traced to an alarm not acted upon.
luna: The section says an alarm is not effective if its hearer turns away; here warning or no warning makes no difference to those who will not believe.
luna: This defines the receptive counterpart to the section’s fire-denier: only one who follows the reminder and fears the Merciful is warned in a beneficial sense.
terra: The people are told to take protective heed of what lies before and behind them so that they may receive mercy, framing taqwā as spatial precaution against approaching danger.
terra: No sign comes from their Lord without their turning away from it, supplying the failed response to the precautionary alarm in 36:45.
terra: “This is the Hell you were promised” identifies the warned object immediately before 36:64 orders the deniers to enter it.
terra: ٱصْلَوْهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ orders entry into Hell because of disbelief, joining the section's ص ل ي action to rejection of the warning.
terra: The wrongdoers, their counterparts, and what they worship are gathered together before 37:23 directs them to Hell's path, supplying the company being marched toward that destination.
terra: “Guide them to the path of Hellfire” turns direction itself into an arrival at fire, illuminating the section's paradox of being facilitated along the difficult, twisted route.
terra: Fire covers the condemned above and below, and God says ذَٰلِكَ يُخَوِّفُ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦ عِبَادَهُۥ ... فَٱتَّقُونِ; the frightening fire is itself the alarm that calls forth a shield.

luna: Those who اجتنبوا false gods and turn to God receive good news; this is active avoidance in the source-section root ج ن ب, paired here with a positive outcome. | terra: Those who keep themselves away from false powers and turn to God receive good news; their self-directed اجتناب shows the same distancing motion that the wretched misdirect toward the reminder in 87:11.
terra: The messenger is asked whether he can rescue someone already in the fire after the sentence has taken effect; the impossible rescue contrasts with God's promised warding before entry.
terra: A condemned person tries to يَتَّقِى بِوَجْهِهِۦ the evil punishment with his face; this grotesque last-minute “shield” contrasts with taqwā established before danger.
terra: People are told to follow the best revelation before punishment comes suddenly while they are unaware, stating the practical precaution that must follow warning.

luna: God delivers those who fear Him and evil does not touch them; this states the section’s protective result in the same fearful group. | terra: God delivers ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوا۟ so that evil does not touch them; this makes their prior taqwā and God's subsequent rescue the two actions joined in the section.

luna: Hell’s keepers ask whether warners came, and the disbelievers admit the warning; this joins the section’s alarm to the fire it announces. | terra: At Hell's opened gates its keepers ask the arriving companies whether messengers came reciting signs and warning them; their admission reproduces the section's warning-before-entry sequence.

luna: The deniers are told to enter Hell and remain there, the outcome opposite the section’s pious person kept from it. | terra: They are told to enter Hell's gates and remain there, contributing the actual admission and permanence after the warning inquiry of 39:71.

luna: Those who feared their Lord are led to the Garden instead, completing the section’s contrast between ashqa and atqa. | terra: Those who practiced taqwā are conducted to the Garden in groups, forming the protected counterpart to the groups driven to Hell after their warning in 39:71-72.
luna: The Garden’s residents praise God for fulfilling His promise; this completes the rescue side of the fire/Garden contrast begun in 39:73.

luna: The angels ask God to protect believers from the punishment of Hell; this prayer states the section’s shield image as a plea for protection. | terra: The bearers of the Throne pray وَقِهِمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ for those who repent and follow God's way, directly asking God to perform the warding pictured in the section.
luna: The same prayer asks that believers enter gardens, completing the escape from fire with the opposite destination.

luna: The prayer asks God to protect them from evil deeds; this matches the source-section root و ق ي as making a barrier against what is feared. | terra: وَقِهِمُ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ broadens the same shield from Hell's fire to the evil acts and consequences that lead there, explaining what may be intercepted before the final danger.

luna: The believer in Pharaoh’s court says he calls his people to salvation while they call him to the Fire, making the section’s warning choice explicit. | terra: The believing man asks why he calls his people to salvation while they call him to the fire, stating the section's opposed directions as rival spoken appeals.

luna: God protects the believer from Pharaoh’s plotting, a concrete use of the source section’s protection idea before the contrasting punishment. | terra: فَوَقَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِ مَا مَكَرُوا shows God actively warding the believing man from a hostile plot, while 40:46 supplies the fire that engulfs Pharaoh's people instead.

luna: Pharaoh’s people are exposed to the Fire morning and evening and then enter harsher punishment, opposite the person God protects in 40:45. | terra: Pharaoh's people are exposed to the fire morning and evening and then ordered into the severest punishment; it completes 40:45's contrast between one person warded and his attackers enclosed by fire.

terra: When the people turn away, the messenger says he has warned them of a thunderbolt like those of ʿAd and Thamud; the threatened object differs from fire, but the immediate turn-away after a specific alarm matches the section's failed response.
terra: Whether the condemned endure patiently or not, the fire remains their dwelling and no appeal restores favor; this makes endurance powerless once the alarm has been ignored.

luna: The verse contrasts the person cast into Fire with the one who comes safe on Judgment Day, closely matching the section’s wretch entering fire and the mindful person kept from it. | terra: One person is cast into the fire while another arrives secure on Resurrection Day, setting fiery admission and protected arrival side by side.
terra: The revelation warns the central city and those around it of the gathering day, when one group is in the Garden and another in the blaze; warning and the two destinations are stated together.
terra: The criminals remain in Hell's punishment, a direct statement of the lasting residence contained in the section's ص ل ي gloss.
terra: The punishment is not lightened and they despair within it, adding unrelieved severity to 43:74's permanence.

luna: The dwellers of the Garden are protected from the punishment of Hell; this is another direct use of the source-section root و ق ي for the pious kept away from fire. | terra: After saying the blessed will taste no further death, وَوَقَىٰهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ names divine warding as the reason the fire never becomes their abiding place.

luna: The disbelievers are brought to the Fire after enjoying worldly life and acting arrogantly; this makes a specific link between the section’s fire-bound person and the preference for nearer life described in 87:16.
luna: The command to remind with the Quran is directed to one who fears God’s warning, matching the section’s contrast between the fearful recipient and the wretch.
luna: This repeats Abraham’s حنيذ calf; it activates the source-section root ص ل ي’s cooking sense as a contrast to entering the blazing fire.
terra: فَفِرُّوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ إِنِّى لَكُم مِّنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ gives the warning its proper completion: hearing the alarm produces immediate movement toward safety.
luna: The deniers are pushed toward Hell, a forceful entry scene for the fire that the section warns about.

luna: They are told that this is the Fire they used to deny, matching the section’s sequence from warning to denial and punishment. | terra: The condemned are told, “This is the fire you used to deny,” placing denial and the now-visible warned object in one confrontation.
luna: The inmates are asked whether the punishment is magic or whether they cannot see, continuing the exposure of the fire-deniers.

luna: The command to burn in it uses the source-section root ص ل ي and directly describes enduring the flame. | terra: ٱصْلَوْهَا فَٱصْبِرُوٓا۟ أَوْ لَا تَصْبِرُوا۟ makes entering the fire and enduring it explicit, closely matching the section's gloss of ص ل ي as suffering its heat and severity.
luna: The muttaqin are placed in gardens and bliss, the other side of the section’s wretch who enters fire.

luna: This says their Lord protected them from the punishment of Hell, a direct example of the section’s shield for the God-fearing. | terra: وَوَقَىٰهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ states the section's two-stage protection directly: their Lord, rather than they themselves, wards the blaze away.
terra: The saved speakers say God favored them and وَوَقَىٰنَا عَذَابَ ٱلسَّمُومِ, presenting rescue from scorching punishment as a received shield.
luna: The person who turns away from the reminder and wants only worldly life matches the section’s denier who turned away before facing the fire.
luna: Lot warned his people of God’s assault, but they disputed the warnings; this is the section’s unheeded alarm in a specific prophetic scene.
luna: The people of the left are given shade of black smoke; this apparent shelter is the opposite of the section’s protective shield, and the next verse states its failure.
luna: That smoke-shade is neither cool nor beneficial, completing the failed-shelter image that reverses the section’s siper.
terra: The question “Have you considered the fire you kindle?” directs attention to fire itself, preparing its surprising function as a reminder in 56:73.
terra: God asks whether people created its tree or He did, shifting kindled fire from a human tool to a divinely supplied sign before 56:73 names its purpose.
terra: “We made it a reminder and a provision for travelers” makes ordinary fire both alarm and benefit, a revealing counterpart to the section's warned blaze.
luna: The passage identifies the condemned person as an astray denier, matching the section’s wretch who denied the warning before entering fire.
luna: This denier’s reception is boiling water, the next stage of the punishment described before the burning in 56:94.
luna: The verse names burning in Hell, using the source-section root ص ل ي and joining denial to fire.

luna: A wall with a door divides believers inside mercy from hypocrites outside with punishment; it makes the section’s separating shield a visible boundary between different ends. | terra: A wall is placed between believers and hypocrites, with mercy inside and punishment outside; it is a literal intervening layer that sorts who is sheltered from the threatened side.

terra: Those outside the wall are told that they tempted themselves, waited, doubted, and were deceived until God's command came, explaining the failed precaution that placed them on 57:13's punishment side.
terra: The hypocrites find no ransom and their refuge is the fire, completing 57:13's wall scene by identifying the punishment outside it.
luna: They take oaths as جُنَّة, a shield, then turn from God’s path and face punishment; unlike the section’s true taqwa barrier, this shield is deceptive and does not protect.

terra: The expelled people thought their fortresses would protect them, but judgment reached them from where they did not expect; the failed external barrier clarifies why the section locates effective protection in taqwā and God's warding.

luna: The verse says whoever is protected from his own شح succeeds; the section opposes the miser with the one who gives and is spared the Fire. | terra: وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِۦ makes greed an inward danger from which one must be shielded; because the ayah praises giving preference to others, it identifies a barrier that precedes the section's fire-shield.
terra: Each soul is commanded to inspect what it has sent ahead for tomorrow while repeating the call to taqwā, explicitly making foresight and preparation the response to future danger.
luna: The same false shield of oaths is used while they deny and block God’s path; it contrasts the section’s protective taqwa with a cover that leads toward punishment.

terra: After commanding taqwā, listening, obedience, and giving, the ayah says whoever is shielded from the self's greed succeeds; it joins the section's giving and protective roots inside one moral sequence.

luna: The command قوا أنفسكم asks people to protect themselves and their families from Fire, directly matching the section’s self-placement within a shield. | terra: قُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارًا turns the dictionary's protective layer into an active duty: build protection for oneself and one's household before the fire is reached.
terra: Those cast into Hell hear it inhaling while it boils, supplying the moving and sounding flame just before 67:8 calls it nearly split by rage and asks about warning.

luna: The section says the fire can be angry; here Hell nearly bursts from الغيظ and its keepers ask whether a نذير came, joining the raging fire and warning in one scene. | terra: The section joins an enraged fire, entry into it, and a warning; here Hell nearly bursts with rage and every arriving company is asked whether a warner came, making the whole alarm-to-fire sequence explicit.

luna: The section’s alarm is meant to produce precaution, but these inmates say a نذير came and they كذبنا; the next ayah supplies the raging fire that receives them. | terra: The entrants admit that a warner did come but that they denied him; this supplies the exact failed response to the section's فَأَنذَرْتُكُمْ and its denier.
terra: The condemned say that had they listened or reasoned they would not be companions of the blaze, stating precisely the precautionary step omitted after the warning of 67:8-9.
terra: The one walking fallen on his face is contrasted with one walking upright on a straight path, supplying the bodily geometry behind the section's twisted route and its need for straightening.
luna: The condemned person is seized and bound, a concrete beginning to the punishment of the wretch who enters the section’s fire.

luna: He is ordered into Hell, completing the seizure in 69:30 with the section’s central fire outcome. | terra: ثُمَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ orders the denier into the blaze, using the same entry-and-burning root as the section.

luna: The condemned did not believe in God, matching the section’s denied warning before the fire. | terra: The person sent into the blaze did not believe in God, supplying refusal as one cause of 69:31's fiery entry.

luna: He did not urge feeding the poor, a specific reversal of the giving that marks the section’s protected side. | terra: He also did not urge feeding the poor, placing refusal to give beside entry into the blaze and thereby reversing the section's protected giver.
luna: The sinner’s food in punishment is described as foul, continuing the fire-bound fate after the denial and withheld charity in 69:33–34.
luna: Only sinners eat that punishment food, completing the section’s identification of the wretched person with the fire-bound end.

luna: The source section names لظى as the fire’s name and glosses its root as pure flame; this verse identifies the fire as لظى. | terra: إِنَّهَا لَظَىٰ uses the section's flame-word as Hell's proper name, confirming that تَلَظَّىٰ evokes both blazing action and a named destination.

luna: The section explains ص ل ي through enduring fire and roasting; لظى here is described as stripping the flesh of the scalp, a specific bodily effect of the flame. | terra: Lezā is described as stripping away the skin or scalp, giving the named pure flame of 70:15 a bodily action before it calls the one who turned away in 70:17.

luna: The section says the fire calls the one who turned away; this verse repeats أدبر وتولى as the person Leza calls, directly connecting rejection to the flame. | terra: Lezā تَدْعُوا۟ مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ; the fire itself summons the one who turned his back, exactly joining the section's blazing fire to the posture of turning away from its alarm.

luna: The source section quotes this exact continuation: Leza calls the one who جمع فأوعى, joining the fire with the gatherer who hoards. | terra: Lezā calls the one who gathered and hoarded, tying the named flame to the withholding of wealth that stands opposite the section's protected giver.
luna: The human who is stingy when good reaches him sharpens the section’s contrast between the miser and the most mindful person spared from fire.
luna: The righteous have a known share in their wealth, contrasting with the gatherer who hoards in 70:18 and the section’s fire-bound miser.
luna: The wealth share is for the asker and deprived, specifying the giving that opposes the hoarding named just before the section’s fire scene.
luna: The righteous affirm the Day of Judgment, the opposite of the section’s person who denies and turns away before the warning.
luna: They fear their Lord’s punishment, giving the fear that motivates the section’s shield against the threatened fire.
luna: The passage says no one is secure from the Lord’s punishment; this makes the section’s protective taqwa a needed response to the fire warning.
luna: Noah is told to warn his people before painful punishment comes, a direct formulation of the section’s alarm before the fire.
luna: Noah identifies himself as a clear warner, matching the section’s single voice that delivers the signal.
luna: The warning’s requested response is to worship, fear God, and obey; the section says alarm is completed when hearers take precaution.
luna: The warning is followed by promised forgiveness and a deferred appointed term, showing what responding to the alarm may avert.
terra: Those who submit تَحَرَّوْا۟ رَشَدًا, deliberately seeking right direction; 72:15 then makes the deviating group fuel for Hell, closely joining straight course and fiery end.
terra: The قَاسِطُونَ, those who deviate, become firewood for Hell, a concrete parallel to the section's crooked course arriving at the craftsman's fire.
terra: The trumpet's day is called يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ, bringing the section's hardship word into the same surah that presents Saqar as a warning.
terra: That day is “not easy” for the unbelievers, explicitly opposing عَسِير to ease and clarifying who experiences the section's destination of hardship.

luna: The source-section root ص ل ي describes entering fire; this verse threatens to cast the denier into Saqar. | terra: God says He will burn the rejecting man in Saqar, a direct use of the section's fire-entry root within the passage that later calls Saqar a warning to humanity.
luna: Saqar neither spares nor leaves anything, specifying the severity of the fire the section warns about.
luna: The section glosses تلظى as pure flame and ص ل ي as enduring heat; here the fire scorches human skin.
terra: Saqar is declared one of the greatest things, establishing the immense fire whose function the next ayah identifies as warning humankind.
terra: نَذِيرًا لِّلْبَشَرِ makes the fire described in the surrounding passage itself a warning, collapsing the section's alarm and its fiery object into one sign.
luna: The question asks what brought the speakers into Saqar, framing the specific failures that follow as causes of entering fire.
luna: The inmates say they did not feed the poor; this reverses the giver whom the whole surah 92 sets against its miser, in the section’s fire-bound division.
luna: They say they denied the Day of Judgment, directly matching the section’s person who denied and turned away before being warned of fire.

luna: The people who give food to the poor, orphan, and captive set up the righteous action that precedes protection from the Day’s evil in 76:11, as in the section’s giving and taqwa. | terra: The protected people of 76:11 first give food despite loving it, so their warding is tied to the same giving posture that precedes taqwā in the section.

luna: They say they feed only for God’s face and seek neither reward nor thanks, matching the section’s giving for God rather than repayment. | terra: They say they feed only for وَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ and seek no return, supplying the face-of-God motive that links the section's giver to the protection in 76:11.

luna: Their reason for feeding is fear of a grim day; this links the section’s protective taqwa to the fear that moves one to give. | terra: Their giving is accompanied by fear of a grim day; this ayah supplies the feared object against which God's warding in 76:11 answers.

luna: The source section explicitly cites this root و ق ي: God protects them from the evil of that day after their God-directed giving. | terra: فَوَقَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ شَرَّ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمِ makes God the agent who places protection around the givers described in 76:8-10, matching the section's move from self-protective taqwā to divine warding.
luna: After God protects the givers from the Day’s evil in 76:11, this verse gives them gardens and silk, completing the protective reward linked to the section’s giver.
luna: The condemned are told to go to a three-branched shade, a supposed shelter inside the fire scene that the next verse exposes as no refuge.

luna: The shade neither cools nor protects from flame; it is the direct reversal of the source-section’s siper, a shelter that fails against the danger. | terra: The smoke offers لَا ظَلِيلٍ وَلَا يُغْنِى مِنَ ٱللَّهَبِ: a seeming cover that neither shades nor protects from flame, exposing a false shield at the very edge of fire.
luna: The same fire throws sparks like great palaces, giving the moving, vivid flame that the source glosses for تلظى.
luna: The next verse compares the sparks with yellow camels, continuing the section’s image of flame as rapidly moving fire.
luna: Hell is called a مرصاد for the transgressors, a waiting place for the person whose turn-away leads to fire in the section.
luna: The transgressors remain in Hell for ages; this matches the source-section explanation that entering fire can mean remaining bound to it.
luna: These people did not expect an account, a concrete form of the denial that precedes the section’s threatened Fire.
luna: They rejected God’s signs, matching the section’s one who كذب and turned away before entering fire.
luna: The inmates are told to taste punishment that only increases, specifying the severity behind the section’s warning.
luna: The next passage gives the God-fearing success, the opposite group to the transgressors for whom Hell is a waiting place.
luna: The God-fearing receive a reward from their Lord; this completes the protective destination introduced for them in 78:31.

luna: The verse says “We warned you” of near punishment and makes the threatened day concrete; it echoes the section’s warning of an approaching fire and reckoning. | terra: إِنَّا أَنذَرْنَاكُمْ عَذَابًا قَرِيبًا warns of a near punishment on the day each person sees what his hands sent ahead, making the alarm an occasion for action before arrival.

luna: The section warns of a fire; here Hell is made visible to whoever sees, a direct scene of the threatened fate being shown. | terra: Hell is made visible to whoever sees, beginning a judgment scene that sorts the one who preferred the nearer life from the one who feared and restrained himself.

luna: The section’s ashqa enters the fire; this passage begins its matching account with the one who transgressed. | terra: The person whose refuge becomes Hell first transgresses, contributing the initiating act before 79:38 names preference for the nearer life and 79:39 names the fire.

luna: The section’s wretch turns away from the warning; here the transgressor is defined by preferring الحياة الدنيا. | terra: The transgressor prefers ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا, giving the choice that makes Hell his shelter in 79:39 and reversing the section's prior precaution.

luna: This names Hell as the transgressor’s abode, the reverse of the section’s person who is kept away from fire. | terra: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ makes fire the transgressor's enclosing refuge, a grim inversion of the protective shelter sought by taqwā.

luna: This gives the opposite disposition to the wretch: one who fears standing before his Lord and restrains the soul from desire. | terra: The other person fears standing before his Lord and restrains the self from desire, supplying the inward precaution that leads away from 79:39's fire.

luna: The one who fears has the Garden as abode; this is the positive destination corresponding to the section’s al-atqa being removed from the fire. | terra: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ gives the fearful person a true refuge opposite the fire-refuge of 79:39.
terra: The wicked burn in Hell on the Day of Judgment, using the section's ص ل ي root for their actual entry into fire.
terra: They are never absent from that fire, adding the permanence contained in the section's explanation of entering and staying.
terra: Those veiled from their Lord then burn in Hell, using the same root for entry while adding exclusion from divine presence as the condition preceding it.

luna: The source-section root ص ل ي is used here for entering a blazing fire, سعيرًا, after judgment. | terra: The one receiving the record behind the back cries for destruction and burns in a blaze, another contextualized occurrence of the section's ص ل ي action.

luna: The section contrasts the one protected from fire with the wretch; here the reminder benefits من يخشى, the one who fears, identifying who can receive the alarm. | terra: سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَن يَخْشَىٰ says the one who fears will take the reminder, supplying the successful hearing-and-precaution response opposite 87:11's avoidance.

luna: The source-section root ج ن ب describes moving someone away from harm; here the same form yetجنبها says the most wretched avoids the reminder, the reverse of the pious person being kept from fire in 92:17. | terra: وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا ٱلْأَشْقَى makes the most wretched avoid the reminder, whereas the section's most wary is made to avoid the fire; the shared distancing verb exposes the decisive difference in what each person puts aside.

luna: The section’s root ص ل ي explains entering and enduring fire; this verse says the reminder-avoider يَصْلَى النار الكبرى. | terra: The same ٱلْأَشْقَى then يَصْلَى ٱلنَّارَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ, directly pairing the section's wretched person with entering and enduring fire.

luna: This completes 87:12’s fire scene: its entrant neither dies nor lives there, specifying the cost of the wretch’s avoidance of reminder. | terra: The one inside the greatest fire neither dies nor lives, clarifying the continuing condition entailed by 87:12's يَصْلَى.
luna: The section pairs the spared أَتْقَى with giving and self-purification; this adjoining contrast says the one who تزكى succeeds.
luna: The passage says people prefer the nearer life after describing the reminder-avoiding wretch; this makes explicit the preference behind the section’s turning away from warning and its fire.
luna: The Hereafter is better and more lasting, completing 87:16’s contrast and clarifying why the section’s fire warning concerns a lasting end.

luna: This uses the source-section root ص ل ي directly: the condemned face enters نارًا حامية, a hot fire. | terra: Humbled faces burn in an intensely hot fire, a compact repeated formulation of the section's entry verb together with the heat it must endure.
luna: The command to remind matches the section’s alarm; it establishes that the messenger’s role is to recall, leaving the hearer’s response consequential.
luna: The messenger is not a controller over them; that specifies the limit of the section’s warning voice, whose alarm cannot itself make the hearer take precaution.
luna: The person who turns away and disbelieves is the section’s 92:16 figure, specified here as one who leaves the reminder.
luna: This gives the consequence of turning away in 88:23: God subjects that person to the greatest punishment, completing the warning sequence.
luna: The people fail to urge feeding the poor, reversing the giving that marks the protected side of the section’s surah 92 contrast.
luna: They consume inheritance greedily, extending the passage’s indictment of wealth-seeking before the Fire is brought near.
luna: Their immense love of wealth specifies the worldly attachment behind the section’s gatherer who hoards before Leza calls.
luna: Hell is brought near on that Day, completing the wealth indictment with the same approaching fire threatened in the section.
luna: The person regrets not having sent deeds ahead for his life, sharpening the warning that worldly wealth cannot avail at the fall.
luna: The source-section root ش ق و names both wretchedness and hardship; this earlier context sets فُجورها against تقواها before the chapter names its most wretched person.
luna: The section opposes الأشقى to الأتقى; this same surah says the one who تزكى succeeds, giving the counter-side to its named wretch.
luna: The source section makes the most wretched the one led to hardship; here the one who دسّاها fails, opposite the soul that purified itself in 91:9.
luna: Thamud’s denial is stated immediately before the rise of their most wretched person in 91:12, completing the section’s link between the ashqa and rejected warning.

luna: The source section explicitly links its الأشقى to 91:12; the verse names the one who rises among Thamud as أَشْقَاهَا, putting the label in a concrete story. | terra: إِذِ ٱنۢبَعَثَ أَشْقَىٰهَا names Thamud's most wretched member immediately before the denial in 91:14, giving the section's ٱلْأَشْقَى a concrete predecessor.
luna: This is the command that precedes the people’s denial in 91:14: the Messenger names God’s she-camel and her drink, completing what the wretch and his people reject.

luna: The section’s warned person كَذَّبَ and turned away; here the people كَذَّبُوهُ and hamstrung the she-camel after the Messenger’s command. | terra: فَكَذَّبُوهُ records Thamud's denial of its messenger beside 91:12's “most wretched,” so the section's wretched denier repeats the closing movement of the preceding surah.

luna: The source-section dictionary glosses عسر as bending or opposition and links it to the route made difficult; this verse pairs العسر with ease, a counterpoint to the section’s turn toward hardship.
luna: The repeated promise that ease accompanies العسر preserves the section’s named hardship root while offering its opposite outcome.
luna: Pursuit of greater accumulation distracts people, echoing the section’s gatherer who hoards before Leza calls him.
luna: The accumulation continues until visiting the graves, carrying the section’s warning toward the afterlife.
luna: The accumulators are told they will see Hell, a direct consequence after the section’s hoarder and fire warning.
luna: They see it with certainty, intensifying the threatened fire from 102:6.
luna: They will be questioned about نعيم, giving an accounting after the section’s reminder that wealth does not avail at the fall.

luna: The person who counts and hoards wealth matches the gatherer whom Leza calls in the section’s quoted 70:18. | terra: The person who gathers and repeatedly counts wealth supplies the withholding posture whose destination is God's kindled fire in 104:6.
luna: He supposes his wealth will make him immortal, specifying the self-sufficiency that the section sets against fearing the warning.
luna: The hoarder is thrown into the Crusher, directly joining the wealth image to a fire fate.

luna: The Crusher is called نار الله الموقدة, connecting the section’s pure flame and fiery warning with a fire kindled by God. | terra: نَارُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُوقَدَةُ gives the hoarder's destination as God's kindled fire, joining withheld wealth to active ignition.

luna: The fire rises over hearts, specifying the reach of the section’s dangerous flame. | terra: God's kindled fire rises over the hearts, adding an inward reach to the hoarder's fire before 104:8 closes it over them.

luna: The fire is closed over the condemned, reversing the section’s protective enclosure around the God-fearing. | terra: The fire is مُؤْصَدَةٌ عَلَيْهِم, closed over them, making the enclosing layer itself punishment rather than protection.

luna: The closing fire is extended in columns, completing the confinement scene of 104:8. | terra: The fire is closed over them in extended columns, completing the enclosure announced in 104:8 with the structure that seals it.
terra: سَيَصْلَىٰ نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ combines the section's entry verb with a fire characterized by flame, bringing ص ل ي and its “pure flame” explanation into one wording.
